# Brain, kidney and liver

[All modules](README.md) · [Known misses](../validation/known-misses.md#organs) · 14 source files, 1664 lines · 30 test files

## Purpose

<!-- hand:purpose -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

This module models three organs the monitor does not draw directly but the scenario depends on. The brain computes
intracranial pressure, cerebral blood flow, brain oxygen and the ICP waveform, and raises the Cushing response; the
kidney computes renal blood flow, glomerular filtration and urine output; the liver sets hepatic flow and its share of
lactate clearance. A clinician-educator reads it to see how ICP, CPP and urine output answer pressure, CO2 and drugs;
an embedding developer reads it for the organ inputs it collects and the effects it hands back to the circulation.
<!-- /hand:purpose -->

## Equations in words

<!-- hand:equations -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

- ICP rises exponentially with the change in intracranial volume, ICP = ICP0·10^(ΔV/PVI), the volume summing mass,
  oedema, cerebral blood volume, displaced CSF, osmotic water loss and head-up drainage, with Marmarou CSF dynamics
  (tables §5.1; `l2/brain/mechanics.ts`).
- Cerebral blood flow is CBF0 × autoregulation of CPP × CO2 reactivity × an O2 term × flow–metabolism coupling, with
  pressure-passive flow when autoregulation is lost; CO2 reactivity is linear in PaCO2 over 20–80 mmHg (tables §5.1;
  `l2/brain/flow.ts`).
- Cerebral blood volume follows Grubb's relation, CBV ∝ CBF^0.38 (tables §5.1; `l2/brain/params.ts`); the head
  sees MAP − 0.74·h when raised (tables §5.1; `l2/brain/params.ts`).
- Brain tissue O2 rises with the delivery-to-demand ratio to the power 0.75, and jugular saturation is SaO2 × (1 − OER)
  with extraction rising as delivery falls, capped at 0.75 (`l2/brain/flow.ts`, `l2/brain/params.ts`).
- The Cushing response starts when CPP stays below 40 mmHg or the ICP comes within 10 mmHg of head MAP for over
  30 s; its drive raises MAP by up to 50 mmHg, slows the heart by up to 40 % and drives ataxic breathing (tables §5.1;
  `l2/brain/cushing.ts`, `l2/organs/effects.ts`).
- The ICP waveform is three Gaussians per perfused beat (percussion, tidal, dicrotic) plus a respiratory component
  (tables §5.1; `l2/brain/wave.ts`).
- The kidney is one algebraic circuit: renal blood flow is the pressure drop over the summed resistances, and
  GFR = Kf·(P_gc − P_B − π̄), with the mean glomerular oncotic pressure rising with filtration fraction (Deen,
  Robertson & Brenner 1972; research/13; tables §5.2; `l2/renal/kidney.ts`).
- Pressure natriuresis scales the excreted fraction so urine output triples from a renal arterial pressure of 100 to
  150 mmHg (Guyton's renal output curve via the tables; after Pulse; `l2/renal/params.ts`); furosemide acts through an
  Emax effect on its plasma level (`l2/renal/model.ts`, `l2/renal/params.ts`).
- Hepatic flow falls with sympathetic constriction, α-agonists, volatiles and an outflow pressure above 5 mmHg, and
  liver failure lowers the liver's share of lactate clearance (tables §5.3; research/13; Diebel 1992;
  `l2/liver/liver.ts`).
<!-- /hand:equations -->
